- With another provider registered under the name "BC", as Android 4.1 does with its bundled BC 1.46, a certificate parsed by an unregistered BouncyCastleProvider took its signature algorithm name from that provider, and the BCJSSE trust manager then rejected a valid sha256WithRSAEncryption chain because "SHA256WithRSAEncryption" matched no supported signature scheme. Certificate and CRL signature algorithm names now come from a BouncyCastleProvider (the registered one, or a private instance), and the BCJSSE algorithm checks name the RSA PKCS#1 v1.5, ECDSA, DSA and SM2 certificate signature algorithms from the OID rather than from X509Certificate.getSigAlgName() (github #2506).

- DESedeParameters.isWeakKey(key, offset, length) compared the loop position against the length rather than offset + length, so at a non-zero offset it stopped early and missed a weak key in the later parts; with an offset of 8, a weak third key was not reported by either overload. isRealEDEKey(key, offset) likewise chose between the two and three part checks from the array length alone, so a two part key at a non-zero offset was checked as a three part one and threw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; the key is now taken to run from the offset to the end of the array. Callers within BC always pass an offset of 0 and were unaffected (github #2548).

- ECPoint.hashCode() hashed the representation of its field elements, so a point on one of the optimised custom curves and the same point on the generic curve were equal but had different hash codes. As a result an EC public key generated with initialize(192), initialize(256) or prime256v1 was equal to its decoded copy, and to the same key with explicit parameters, but not found in a HashSet holding it. Points now hash their coordinate values (github #2545).

+- ASN1InputStream.readObject() turned an IllegalArgumentException into an ASN1Exception only for definite-length encodings, so malformed content inside an indefinite-length constructed encoding, such as a bad BIT STRING in a BER SEQUENCE, SET or tagged object, escaped as an unchecked IllegalArgumentException or IllegalStateException through parsers such as CMSSignedData, OCSPResp, TimeStampResponse and PKCS10CertificationRequest that declare only checked exceptions. Both are now reported as an ASN1Exception for either form. The same malformed BIT STRING content also escaped unchecked from ASN1StreamParser, whose BIT STRING parser threw IllegalArgumentException and IllegalStateException from getLoadedObject() and getBitStream() despite both declaring IOException; it now throws ASN1Exception, as does the EXTERNAL parser for an EXTERNAL holding an implicitly tagged object, and the streaming CMS parsers no longer let malformed content out unchecked: CMSSignedDataParser in the digestAlgorithms, certificates or CRLs, CMSEnvelopedDataParser and CMSAuthenticatedDataParser in the recipientInfos, the attribute getters of the enveloped, authenticated and auth-enveloped parsers (including an attribute set element that is not an Attribute), and CMSTimeStampedDataParser in the metaData or temporal evidence, or for an absent evidence block or the wrong content type. The EnvelopedData, AuthEnvelopedData and AuthenticatedData stream parsers now also report an attribute set with the wrong tag, or a mac that is not an OCTET STRING, as an IOException. Separately, CMSAuthenticatedDataParser.getUnauthAttrs() called before getMac() read the authenticated attributes or the mac in place of the unauthenticated attributes and failed on a valid message; it now reads past both first (github #2547).
